note: GIT COMMIT ON macOS CAN TAKE HOURS, IN BASH, WITH NO COMPILER RUNNING - AND ps WILL NOT SHOW IT. The pre-commit hook runs gate-commit, which enters scripts/subfloor-run-chunked.sh, whose line ~103 does a bash parameter substitution over the 229,189-byte subfloor filter. Under macOS stock bash 3.2 that is roughly O(n^3). Measured on ambrose, same filter truncated: 5,000 B = 0s, 10,000 B = 1s, 20,000 B = 8s, 40,000 B = 59s, about 7.5x per doubling. IT IS ALSO LOCALE-SENSITIVE, which is the half nobody guesses: at 40,000 bytes LC_ALL=C takes 5s and LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 takes 62s, a 12x gap, because bash 3.2 pattern-matches multibyte-aware under UTF-8. Extrapolated to the real filter that is roughly 13 min under C and hours under UTF-8. DIAGNOSTIC TRAP THAT COST ME AN HOUR: I probed with ps for cargo and rustc, saw nothing, and concluded a subagent had parked. The work is done by BASH. Probe for bash, or better, grep docs/timings.md for a completed row - timed.sh only writes on completion, so it is the one signal that separates gate-still-running from gate-finished-and-something-else-is-wrong. ZERO-RISK WORKAROUND, no file changed: HV_SUBFLOOR_CHUNK_BYTES is already an env override on the threshold, and Darwin has no per-arg MAX_ARG_STRLEN - getconf ARG_MAX is 1048576 and a 229,189-byte argv arg was verified to pass to an execve child. Prefix the commit with HV_SUBFLOOR_CHUNK_BYTES=400000 and the script takes its own fast path. Verified: commit 716506630 landed with a full green gate. SECOND BASH 3.2 DEFECT THIS SESSION - see post 174e100e, where test-worktree-freshness.sh does not even parse under 3.2. Both are clean under shellcheck and both work on leffords bash 5. The pattern is the finding: repo shell scripts are authored against bash 5 and run unverified on 3.2.
